newsitem.title: UK: UK gilts this week - Mkt may struggle to stay ahead.
newsitem.headline: UK gilts this week - Mkt may struggle to stay ahead.

text.p: UK gilts could struggle to maintain the new highs reached late last week after a U.S.-inspired rally, with little of the upcoming week's domestic data likely to be supportive, analysts said on Monday.
"Gilts are looking a little vulnerable and a chunky retail sales number on Wednesday could reverse their recent good performance," said Kevin Adams, gilts analyst at BZW.
Analysts said the yield spread between 10-year gilts and U.S. T-notes of 100 basis points in particular looks unsustainable.
"That spread is as narrow as it has been for a while. Given the feeling now prevalent that the U.S. economy has slowed down of its own accord, that spread could push back out," Adams said.

U.S. Treasuries forged ahead on Friday after a muted increase in retail sales activity and consumer prices in August eased fears of a near-term U.S. rate rise. U.S. bonds gained nearly two points and gilts a point.
"Gilts were dragged up by the U.S. on Friday, but unless we get some good news of our own I can't see it lasting," said a gilts salesman.
August PSBR data due on Tuesday offers most hope, he said.
"The market got a very good figure for July and is expecting something less favourable this time, but I think it may be pleasantly surprised."
The consensus forecast suggests a borrowing requirement of 4.1 billion stg in August after July's repayment of 1.7 billion.
But the rest of the week's data may underline the British economy's strength, especially in the consumer sector, and give gilts a rough ride.
August retail sales data is forecast to show a 0.5 percent rise and a year-on-year rise of 3.5 percent compared with 2.2 percent in July.
And M4 figures due on Thursday are forecast to show broad money growth stuck stubbornly at 9.0 percent in August, the upper limit of the government's monitoring range.
But BZW's Adams said the market may get some support from Europe even if the data and survey's show renewed economic strength. The German ifo survey due later this week will be a focal point.
"Bond markets could react positively to a strong figure because of Germany needs to see stronger growth to ease its fiscal problems," said Adams.
The meeting this weekend between EU finance ministers in Dublin will help focus the markets' mind on the Maastricht convergence criteria for European monetary union.
Among the issues addressed will be the stability pact on fiscal decifits and the possibility of automatic fines for divergent economies.
Gilt futures clung to Friday's gains in early Monday trading, the December contract stood at 108-00.
But the gilts salesman said if the future breaks above 108-00, he has a batch of sell orders to place in the market.
"There are a lot of investors seeking to move a bit shorter and 108-00 is the level they want to sell at," he said.
The yield curve has been steady over the last week with only the five-year area cheapening slightly.
But one trader at a GEMM said the best area remains 10-years. "That will avoid any problems at the short end if interest rate expectations radically alter after the retail sales data," he said.
And the gilts market could be undermined further if the FTSE index of 100 leading shares continues to make new record highs.
"There has been a lot of shifting out of gilts and into equities over the last three months and that shows no signs of abating," the salesman said.
